newsitem.title: USA: Ascend tumbles, dragging tech stocks, Nasdaq lower.
newsitem.headline: Ascend tumbles, dragging tech stocks, Nasdaq lower.

text.p: Shares of Ascend Communications Inc. plunged 13 percent in heavy trading Tuesday as several Wall Street analysts reduced their ratings on the company, citing near-term earnings risks.
The decline sent a shudder through other computer networking equipment stocks and put pressure on the volatile high-technology sector as a whole, analysts said.

"Ascend put some of the other networking stocks under pressure. Intel's off ... and that was a lot of the OTC (over-the-counter) decline today," said Patrick Davis, head of OTC trading at Salomon Brothers.
Davis said the decline might continue Wednesday.
The Alameda, Calif.-based company's stock was the the most actively traded in the stock market, falling $6.25 to $41.375 on volume of more than 27.8 million shares on Nasdaq.
Semiconductor giant Intel Corp., meanwhile, fell $4.0625 to $145.1875. UBS Securities analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos said he had
lowered his rating on Ascend to a "hold" rating from a "buy" due to near-term risks and uncertainties.
Ascend officials were not immediately available for comment.
Soundview Financial Corp analyst Michael Karfopoulos lowered his short-term rating on Ascend and trimmed his 1997 earnings estimate but maintained his long-term "buy" rating.

Among other networking companies, Cascade Communications Corp., which is expected to complete a merger with Ascend by June 30, fell $4.3125 to $28.5625, while Cisco Systems Inc. slipped $1.50 to $65, both on Nasdaq.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index lost 10.35 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 1,401.69.
Applied Materials Inc. dropped $3.625 to $60.75 on Nasdaq after investment bank Hambrecht & Quist downgraded the stock and two other semiconductor equipment makers.
